questions.questionText: SECTION A - COMPOSITION (20 marks). Choose EITHER Question 1(a) OR Question 1(b). Spend about 1 hour on this section. Write your answer in 80-120 words. Either (a): You have been asked to speak at your school assembly to encourage younger pupils to take care of the environment. Write the speech you will give. Use the following points and any others you may think of: why the environment must be protected; one problem caused by littering or cutting down trees; what pupils can do to help; who can support them (teachers, parents, community leaders); and why this matters for the future.
questions.explanation: Original question, written in the exact real ZIMSEC 7010/2 format (Section A Composition, 20 marks, choice of 2, 80-120 words, guided by bullet points) confirmed from the real specimen paper - not copied from it. Marking guidance (based on real ZIMSEC conventions for this paper type): a suitable heading/title earns 1 mark; candidates must address the SPEECH register (spoken to an audience, e.g. 'Good morning everyone', not written as a letter or story); every bullet point should be addressed with real substance, not just mentioned in passing; good grammar, spelling and punctuation are marked throughout; candidates commonly lose marks by writing a general essay about pollution instead of addressing it AS A SPEECH to a specific audience (their own schoolmates).

questions.questionText: SECTION A - COMPOSITION (20 marks). Choose EITHER Question 1(a) OR Question 1(b). Spend about 1 hour on this section. Write your answer in 80-120 words. Or (b): Write a composition describing a memorable day you spent helping at a family or community event (for example a wedding, a harvest, or a family gathering). Use the following points and any others you may think of: what the event was; where and when it took place; who else was there; what your role or job was on the day; and why you will always remember it.
questions.explanation: Original question, written in the exact real ZIMSEC 7010/2 format - not copied from the real specimen paper. SECTION B - COMPREHENSION (15 marks). Spend about 45 minutes on this section. Read the passage carefully, then answer the questions that follow in full, grammatically correct sentences.

VICTORIA FALLS: THE SMOKE THAT THUNDERS

Victoria Falls is one of Zimbabwe's greatest natural treasures. Local people have long called it "Mosi-oa-Tunya," which means "the smoke that thunders," because the huge cloud of spray rising from the falls can be seen from many kilometres away, and the roar of the crashing water sounds like distant thunder.

The falls were formed over millions of years as the mighty Zambezi River wore away layers of soft rock, leaving behind a deep, narrow gorge with hard basalt walls on either side. Today, the river plunges more than one hundred metres into this gorge, creating one of the largest curtains of falling water found anywhere on Earth.

Every year, thousands of visitors from Zimbabwe and from other countries travel to see the falls. Tourism built around Victoria Falls provides jobs for many local people, who work as tour guides, hotel staff, curio sellers and boat operators. This income helps to support families and to fund the conservation of the surrounding national park.

However, the falls and the wildlife around them face growing threats. Pollution of the Zambezi River, the cutting down of nearby trees, and the effects of changing rainfall patterns all put pressure on this fragile environment. Conservationists warn that without careful management, both the beauty of the falls and the livelihoods that depend on them could be damaged.

Despite these challenges, Victoria Falls remains a proud symbol of Zimbabwe's natural heritage, drawing visitors and admiration from all over the world.

Question (a): Give a metaphor used in paragraph 1 to describe the sound of the falls.
questions.explanation: Original question in the real ZIMSEC comprehension style (figurative language identification, matching the real paper's opening question type). A metaphor describes one thing AS another, directly, without 'like' or 'as' - 'the smoke that thunders' calls the spray 'smoke' outright.

questions.explanation: Original summary question, matching the real ZIMSEC 7010/2 format exactly: 50-word limit, a supplied opening phrase, worth 5 marks. Model marking guidance (in the real ZIMSEC style): award 1 mark for each of up to 5 distinct points selected ONLY from what the question asks for (here: benefits AND threats, not the falls' formation or local name, which are outside this question's scope) - e.g. (1) creates jobs/tourism income, (2) funds conservation, (3) polluted by river pollution, (4) threatened by deforestation, (5) threatened by changing rainfall. questions.questionText:
**Passage:**
The school library had been neglected for several years. Books were dusty, some shelves were broken and many learners preferred to spend their free time outside. A new librarian decided to change the situation. She organised the books, repaired the shelves with the help of the school maintenance team and started a reading club. Within a few months, learners were borrowing books regularly and discussing stories during break time.

Read the passage carefully. Answer the questions that follow. Passage 1.
- (a) Give one reason why the learners initially avoided the library. [1 mark]
- (b) State two actions taken by the new librarian. [2 marks]
- (c) What evidence shows that the changes were successful? [2 marks]
- (d) Give a suitable title for the passage. [1 mark]
questions.explanation:
(a) The books were dusty and some shelves were broken [1 mark].
(b) She organised the books, repaired the shelves, and started a reading club (any two) [2 marks].
(c) Learners began borrowing books regularly and discussing stories during break time [2 marks].
(d) Example: "Reviving the School Library" / "The New Librarian" [1 mark].
